merge.title: Erased-tail check on the selected slot (FSBL boot + CMD_FW_COMMIT), Trezor check_image_contents shape; optionally widen the 8-word fingerprint to the signed manifest digest
merge.threat:
Bytes beyond the manifest-declared image length inside a slot's capacity window are never looked at after ship. fsbl/src/verify.rs:62,68 hashes exactly [base, base+secure_len) and [ns_base, ns_base+ns_len); capacity is only an upper bound (:52-57). secure/src/fw_update/verify.rs:57-58 re-hashes only received_* bytes. secure/src/measured_boot.rs:102-120 hashes [__vector_table, __veneer_limit).

Honest scope, narrower than the members claim:
- Pre-RDP-2 (transit): already covered. The published pre-power SWD diff is a full-flash diff with "unused pages erased 0xFF" (docs/security/user-device-verification.md:85). BOOT-07's "SWD diff stays identical" is false for a transit implant.
- Post-RDP-2: only secure-world code can write a slot. CMD_FW_BEGIN erases every page of the inactive slot (secure/src/hw/flash.rs:1366-1386), and chunk writes are bounded by the declared length.
- What remains: (a) a dormant second-stage left in the ACTIVE slot's tail by a past secure-world memory-safety exploit or updater bug, invisible to the boot fingerprint and surviving reboot; (b) stale bytes of a previous longer image surviving a skipped or glitched page erase at BEGIN, since nothing re-checks the tail at COMMIT; (c) a pre-staged gadget region for a later control-flow fault.
- The Donjon/Rashid "compressible firmware" bypass does NOT apply. It defeats a self-attested hash; pq1's FSBL row is computed by code that is intended to be WRP-frozen.

Separate coverage gap (FWU-4): the rendered 8 words derive from secure_hash only. fsbl/src/verify.rs:109 returns Some(actual_secure), fsbl/src/main.rs:286 renders it, and secure/src/fw_update/mod.rs:135 does the same at install confirm. Two releases differing only in the NS image (USB router, APDU parser) or fw_version show identical words.
merge.proposal:
ONE recommendation in two parts. Part 1 is the cluster core; Part 2 is a separable owner decision.

PART 1 — erased-tail CHECK, not a whole-window HASH.

FSBL (fsbl/src/verify.rs::verify_images):
- After both image hashes pass, word-walk [base+len rounded up to 4, base+CAP) for the secure and NS halves of the SELECTED slot and require every word == 0xFFFF_FFFF.
- Fold the verdict into the existing F15 aggregate (check_true_into_sentinel, verify.rs:102-108), with the walk re-run inside the closure.
- CAP comes from the active geometry via fw_manifest / pqsigner-geometry: legacy 58 and 64 pages (fw-manifest/src/lib.rs:177,180); v6 0x72000 and 0x7A000. Never a second copy of the constant.
- Failure policy: a dirty tail makes the slot INADMISSIBLE (return None), so selection falls through to the other slot exactly like a hash mismatch. No latch, no write, no wipe — consistent with the FSBL's recoverable/never-latch posture (fsbl/src/main.rs:270-280) and the 2026-07-23 halt-never-write decision.

CMD_FW_COMMIT (secure/src/fw_update/verify.rs::verify_images):
- Same walk over the inactive slot's two tails, inside the same four-way sentinel gate. Failure drops the context (FwUpdate error), so a slot that would be refused at boot can never be committed.

Tooling:
- Add the tail-erased assertion to verify-ship-state / the pq1-verify spec (already implied by user-device-verification.md:85; make it explicit and tested).
- Add both walks to the #591 rainbow FI sweep scope.
- Host tests go in a workspace crate, not inside secure/src modules that are cfg(not(test)).
- Re-measure with stage-marker and replace the timing table; do not rescale it.

Why check, not hash:
- It is what Trezor actually ships (image.c:469-500 checks padding; it does not hash it).
- It leaves the signed preimage, fwsign, the published words and the FSBL/secure-world row identity (docs/security/measured-boot.md:228-233) untouched.
- It needs no manifest-v6 change (Draft 1.1 is not implementation-approved).

Boot-time cost — the lead's question:
- Whole-window HASH: 475,136 + 524,288 = 999,424 B against 393,056 B hashed today. At the only silicon-measured rate (software SHA, 1.167 s per 385,568 B, about 330 KB/s) that is about 3.0 s versus 1.19 s, i.e. +1.8 s; FSBL work goes from 2.93 s to about 4.8 s.
- The FSBL has defaulted to the HASH peripheral since c6a97080 (2026-09-28), but that commit states "NOT yet run on silicon". There is no measured HW figure, and the byte-wise read_volatile copy loop (verify.rs:124-136) may dominate either backend.
- Tail CHECK: 606,368 B = 151,592 word loads on the bench image; my estimate is about 0.06-0.1 s single pass at 16 MHz and under 0.2 s double-evaluated (unmeasured). Code cost is an estimated 100-200 B against 10,532 B free in the 32 KiB region.

PART 2 — widen the fingerprint (owner decision, now-or-never before any unit ships).
- Derive the 8 words from the already-computed, already-signature-checked manifest digest (v1: SHA-256(PQFW_V1 || fw_version || secure_hash || ns_hash); v6: the 121-byte preimage) instead of secure_hash.
- Change all three renderers together: FSBL render_fingerprint, secure measured_boot::run, fw_update::confirm_install. Route them through one function in sphincs_tz_bip39 and pin it in fsbl-tests/tests/paired_constants.rs.
- The secure-world row must then read the active manifest's digest. It is already documented as advisory/self-attested, so this loses nothing — but the "same byte range on both rows" section of measured-boot.md must be rewritten in the same change.
- Process half: `make release` emits the expected words per slot into the release record. Slot A and B images are linked at different bases, so there are two word sets per release — true today as well, and v6's physical_slot field makes it explicit. The companion shows them at install.

members.note: Only sub-item (2) belongs here. Kept as the erased-tail CHECK (FSBL + COMMIT). Dropped from it: hashing the window, extending measured_boot::firmware_hash to the same window, and Krux random-fill-and-pin. Sub-items (1), (3), (4) are out of this cluster. Round-1 dispositions stand: (1a) is #46/#270/#387/#595; (1b) on-device OEM-key write contradicts R2.1/C1; (4) wipe-on-mismatch contradicts the 2026-07-23 halt-never-write decision; (3) FSBL RCC_CSR refusal is low value and a brick lever. Round-1 cost correction honoured: the delta is the tail, not ~2x, and the '4 s window' is a hold, not a budget.

Kept: its cheaper alternative — erase-check the remaining words of the slot after hashing. Dropped: (1) full-capacity signed hashes in manifest v6; (2) the expect_erased set for pages outside the registry; (3) Krux first-boot TRNG fill. Its claim that the SWD diff stays identical is wrong pre-RDP-2 (user-device-verification.md:85). Its '2 MB read is cheap' figure is unmeasured; a check is cheap, a hash is +1.8 s at the measured software rate.

Same threat, but its mechanism (hash the full capacity windows into the fingerprint) is replaced by the check. Its cost claim of +0.3-0.5 s is wrong: 606 KB more at 330 KB/s is about +1.8 s. 'With hw-sha256 much less' is unmeasured. Kept: fw_update COMMIT verifies the tail, and verify-ship-state / the RDP-0 verifier assert the same tails. Its premise that the Donjon bypass applies is refuted (FSBL-measured, not self-attested).

Closest to the final shape (word-walk at COMMIT and in the FSBL inside the sentinel gate) — kept. Dropped: the 'sign the lengths' argument. An under-declared secure_len changes the hashed range, so the SHA-256 no longer equals the signed hash; unsigned lengths give no control over where the tail starts, and v6 already signs both lengths (a-b-firmware-rollback-architecture.md:1946-1950). 'len multiple of 16 and >= IMAGE_LEN_MIN' is a v6 format rule, deferred to #540. Its #540 caveat (bank-2 FSBL mirror pages 0..4 inside NS slot A) is confirmed at secure/src/flash_policy.rs:68-73 and kept as a prerequisite.

Distinct idea (what the words cover, not which bytes are checked); kept as Part 2. Code claims confirmed: fsbl/src/verify.rs:109, fsbl/src/main.rs:286, secure/src/fw_update/mod.rs:135, and vendor-signing-key-compromise.md:368-379 already records the finding. Corrections: 'nobody publishes' is partly stale — fwsign erc7730_release_metadata.rs:129-130 already emits secure and NS measurement words, but only for the companion trailer path (tools/companion-stub/erc7730_trailer.py:359), not from the Makefile release flow. Words are per-slot. The secure-world row cannot recompute a manifest digest from its own image, so the row-identity doc must change.

dropped_parts: Whole-window HASH into the fingerprint (IMP-06 (2), SYS-08, BOOT-07 (1)): costs about +1.8 s of FSBL work at the only silicon-measured rate; changes the signed-hash semantics, fwsign padding, the published words and measured_boot::firmware_hash in lockstep; needs manifest work that is not implementation-approved. The check gives the same detection.
Extending measured_boot::firmware_hash to the capacity windows: only needed for the hash variant; that row is self-attested anyway (measured-boot.md).
Krux-style random fill + pinned hash (IMP-06, BOOT-07 (3)): incompatible with a vendor-signed image hash and with the reproducible byte-exact SWD diff; adds per-unit state in page 127.

BOOT-07 (2) expect_erased set for pages 'not owned by the registry': the legacy map has no unowned page (bank 1: FSBL 0-3, manifests 4-5, boot-state 6, slot A 7-64, slot B 65-122, per-device 123-127; bank 2: NS A 0-63, NS B 64-127). The inactive slot is not executed and is fully erased at BEGIN. Pre-ship state is covered by the SWD diff.
FWU-5 'sign the image lengths' as a tail-boundary defence: refuted (hash coverage already binds the length); v6 signs lengths regardless.
IMP-06 (1b) Phase-A OEM key write: recorded decision R2.1/C1 — the only on-device option-byte write is RDP. Out of cluster.
IMP-06 (4) wipe-on-mismatch: owner decision 2026-07-23 (halt, never write); the FSBL has no production flash-write path (fsbl/src/marker.rs fence). Out of cluster.
IMP-06 (3) FSBL refusal on OBLRSTF/IWDG: out of cluster; round-1 found it a brick lever with little gain.
Halt-on-dirty-tail: replaced by slot-inadmissible fall-through, to avoid a permanent brick lever in WRP-frozen code.
FWU-4 claim that the device fingerprint is useless until widened: overstated. A secure-image change is already reflected; only NS-only and version-only differences are invisible.

merge.untracked_delta:
No issue tracks any of the following. I ran 22 searches including tail, whole slot, padding, unmeasured, unused flash, free flash, erased slot, verify_images, secure_len, signed lengths, expected fingerprint and publish fingerprint; the "manifest_digest fingerprint" search returned no rows.
1. Erased-tail check in fsbl::verify_images for the selected slot.
2. Erased-tail check at CMD_FW_COMMIT.
3. Explicit tail-erased assertion in verify-ship-state / pq1-verify.
4. Fingerprint words derived from the signed manifest digest in all three renderers, with a paired-constants pin.
5. `make release` emitting expected words per slot. The VSKC doc recommends it; it has no issue.

File 1-3 as one issue and 4-5 as a second (owner decision).
decision_conflicts: docs/security/measured-boot.md:228-233 ('Same byte range on both rows') makes FSBL/secure-world range identity deliberate. Part 1 as a CHECK does not touch it. Part 2 breaks it unless the secure-world row switches to the manifest digest in the same change — requires an owner decision and a doc rewrite.

Draft 1.1 manifest-v6 is not implementation-approved (CLAUDE.md 'Rollback manifest work is not implementation-approved'). The recommendation therefore avoids any preimage or format change; BOOT-07 (1) and FWU-5's length rules would have required one.

FSBL budget is the recorded NO-GO for rollback work (memory: A/B rollback spec review). Part 1 adds an estimated 100-200 B and under 0.2 s — unmeasured, must be confirmed by make fsbl + stage-marker before landing. The hash variant's +1.8 s would have collided with it.
Invariant #10 / owner decision 2026-07-23: FSBL never writes and never latches. Honoured: the tail verdict is read-only and falls through to the other slot.
The fingerprint word set changes under Part 2. Acceptable only before any device ships; impossible after RDP-2 freezes the FSBL — a now-or-never decision.
prerequisites: Measure before landing: run stage-marker on pq1 for the tail walk. The HW-HASH FSBL (c6a97080) has itself never run on silicon, so the 2.93 s work figure is the software-SHA number.

Confirm on a built ui-px NS image that .pq1a lies inside nonsecure_len. The linker layout says yes (atlas at +0x1000, .text pinned after it at +0x14000; elf-to-bin.sh selects by address) — inferred from the scripts, not from a built binary. If it did not, the tail rule would refuse every ui-px slot.

Geometry: scope the NS walk to the registry's NS slot range and take CAP from fw_manifest / pqsigner-geometry, so the #540/#758 cutover cannot leave the walk covering the bank-2 FSBL mirror or the wrong capacity.

ECC/NMI: the FSBL installs no NMI/ECCD handler (grep of fsbl/src finds none). Reading a torn-erase word raises ECCD; the image-hash read already has this exposure, but the walk enlarges the read area. State the behaviour (default handler = halt = recoverable by power cycle) rather than leave it implicit.
Part 2 only: owner decision on the fingerprint definition; #705 closed for pq1; release process owner for publishing words.

Callers: boardloader/main.c:301 (bootloader area), bootloader/fw_check.c:150,197 (firmware), boardloader/sd_update.c:160. Round 1 dated it to commit 02f34a2748 (2023-10-25) and cites wf_image_upload.c:230-238 for erase-remainder after the last chunk; I did not re-open those two.

Part 2: Trezor's fingerprint is the hash of the whole signature-zeroed header (image.c:168-176), so it covers everything signed; round 1 cites bootui.c for showing it at install. Ledger publishes firmware hashes per release.
merge.rationale:
Priority is P2, not the members' P1.
- No consumer reads tail bytes today: the ui-px atlas sits inside the hashed NS range, and Draft 1.1 already requires the vector and reset targets to lie inside [base, base+len).
- The transit case is covered by the full-flash SWD diff.
- Post-RDP-2, writing a tail already requires secure-world code execution.

The gain is therefore persistence-visibility plus defence in depth against a skipped erase. It is cheap, read-only and vendor-parity, and it must land BEFORE the FSBL is frozen by WRP + RDP-2 because it can never be added afterwards — that deadline is the reason to do it now rather than drop it.

Part 2 is S for firmware plus a process change. It carries the same now-or-never deadline and closes a gap the VSKC review already verified.

Kind is firmware for Part 1; Part 2 adds a release-process half.

live_defects.what: Boot fingerprint covers the secure image only. NS-image-only or fw_version-only differences between two validly signed releases render identical 8 words at boot and at install confirm.
live_defects.reachable_in_production_config: Yes — unconditional code in the FSBL and in confirm_install (only e2e-test short-circuits it). Not a signature bypass: the NS hash is still verified against the signed manifest.
live_defects.severity: low-medium (detection gap, requires a validly signed alternative NS image)

live_defects.what: Slot tail [base+len, base+capacity) is never verified erased at boot or at COMMIT; erase success at BEGIN is the only guarantee.
live_defects.reachable_in_production_config: Yes, but exploiting it needs prior secure-world write capability or a faulted page erase; no current code reads or executes tail bytes.

live_defects.what: Stale documentation in the frozen-range crate: fsbl/src/verify.rs:5-24, fsbl/src/main.rs:40-44 and the fsbl/Cargo.toml dependency note still say the FSBL uses software SHA-256 and that the HASH port is 'not a good trade', while hw-sha256 is the default feature since c6a97080. Round 1's feasibility lens and member SYS-08 each relied on one side of this contradiction.
live_defects.evidence: fsbl/Cargo.toml features block (default = ["hw-sha256"]) versus its own [dependencies] NOTE; fsbl/src/verify.rs:5-24; commit c6a97080 ('NOT yet run on silicon')
live_defects.reachable_in_production_config: Documentation only; the 2.93 s boot-work figure in CLAUDE.md and measured-boot.md is the software-path measurement and is unverified for the current default build.

merge.residual_after:
After Part 1:
- An attacker with secure-world code execution can still hide a payload anywhere the check does not look: per-device pages 123-127, the inactive slot until it is selected, and SRAM.
- The same attacker can lie on the secure-world row.
- A payload can still be placed inside a validly signed image (stolen vendor key): authentic is not benign.
- The check runs only at boot and at COMMIT, so a tail written after boot is live until the next reset.
- A double fault can still skip the sentinel gate (#591 scope).
- A voltage or EM glitch that redirects control flow can still target in-image gadgets.
- Before WRP + RDP-2 close, the FSBL itself is replaceable, so the check is advisory on bench units.
- Not addressed at all: OEM-key planting, option-byte glitching and reset-cause handling (the other IMP-06 sub-items; #46/#270/#595).

After Part 2:
- The words still match a maliciously published release under a compromised key.
- Users must actually compare against an out-of-band published value.
- On pq1 the FSBL row is dark until #705 closes.
- A later fake screen after the boot window remains the accepted residual of invariant #10.

skeptic.reason:
The core survives: an erased-tail CHECK in fsbl::verify_images and at CMD_FW_COMMIT is real, cheap, read-only, untracked, and matches what Trezor ships. I confirmed the code facts by reading them. But the recommendation overstates its safety and its value in six places, so priority drops to P3 for Part 1 and Part 2 should be folded into the manifest-v6 work.

What I confirmed:
- FSBL hashes only [base, base+len); capacity is an upper bound only (fsbl/src/verify.rs:52-68).
- COMMIT re-hashes only received_* bytes (secure/src/fw_update/verify.rs:57-58).
- BEGIN's page erase is judged only by SR error flags, with no blank read-back (secure/src/hw/flash.rs:1307-1352), so threat (b), a skipped or glitched erase leaving a stale tail, is live.
- The final chunk is padded with 0xFF to the 16-byte quadword (secure/src/fw_update/staging.rs:44-92), so a walk from len rounded up to 4 will not false-refuse an honest update.
- Trezor checks padding and does not hash it (image.c:447-449 hashes to codelen; :469+ checks the padding byte).
- No issue tracks the tail check or the fingerprint widening (my searches found none; one search timed out).

Where it fails or overstates:
1. "No brick lever" is false. pick_slot(None, None) halts (fsbl/src/main.rs:220-222, 367-374). A unit as shipped has one valid slot, so a dirty tail there is a permanent halt at RDP-2: CMD_FW_* is the only update path (#696) and it needs a booted image. Fall-through exists only when the other slot is valid.
2. Fall-through is also a forced downgrade. A planted tail in the active slot makes the FSBL boot the previous image, plausibly the vulnerable one the attacker used. An attacker with secure-world write can already force the same by corrupting one image byte, so this is not a new capability, but the check turns stealth persistence into a downgrade or brick, not into a clean detection the user sees.
3. The walk is not confined to the "SELECTED slot". verify_images runs for both A and B before pick_slot (fsbl/src/main.rs:211-212). Placed there, the walk runs on every slot with a valid manifest, each three times (once direct, twice in the sentinel closure). The measured 1.167 s hash figure was taken with manifest B erased (fsbl/src/marker.rs:17,45), so a two-slot device already hashes about twice that. The proposal's "under 0.2 s" should read roughly 0.2-0.5 s, unmeasured.
4. The ECC prerequisite is wrong. The FSBL has no NMI or exception handler (grep of fsbl/src finds none; cortex-m-rt default is a spin loop). A torn-erase page is persistent, so a halt on it repeats every boot; "recoverable by power cycle" does not hold. The walk enlarges the read area from about 393 KB to about 1 MB per slot. Whether an interrupted erase raises ECCD on this silicon is unmeasured.
5. The persistence benefit is small. Unchecked writable space remains in the 8 KiB manifest pages beyond the manifest fields, boot-state page 6, and pages 123-127 (page 125 documents bytes 32..8192 as unused, secure/src/hw/flash.rs:605). A tail payload is inert without a fresh exploit after reboot. The real gains are a smaller gadget field for a control-flow fault (erased flash reads as all-ones, not valid code) and catching a skipped erase.
6. The "now-or-never" deadline applies only to the FSBL half. The COMMIT half lives in updatable secure firmware. The FSBL is being rewritten for #540/manifest-v6 before any unit ships, so the FSBL walk should ride that change, not land as a separate edit of the legacy 32 KiB image.

Part 2 (widen the fingerprint) is valid as an owner decision, but "loses nothing" is wrong. Today the secure-world row independently re-hashes its own image, and CLAUDE.md's Lifecycle section calls honest-row divergence a strong defect/tamper signal. Reading the manifest digest back from flash would turn that row into a copy. To keep the signal the secure world must recompute the digest from its own image hash plus a fresh NS hash plus fw_version, which costs boot time and needs a fallback for monolithic bench builds that have no manifest. The security gain is modest: the NS world is untrusted by design (invariant #4), and an attacker with the vendor key would change the secure image anyway. The value is release identification, not attack detection.
skeptic.corrections:
1. Brick lever: replace "no brick lever / falls through like a hash mismatch" with the true behaviour. With one valid slot (the ship state) a dirty tail halts permanently at RDP-2. Require the #696 bootable-fallback proof to cover the FSBL tail refusal, not only COMMIT.
2. Downgrade: add to the residual that a planted tail forces boot of the previous image when one exists.
3. Scope and cost: verify_images runs on both slots before pick_slot (fsbl/src/main.rs:211-212). Either accept the walk on every valid-manifest slot, three evaluations each, or restructure to check after pick with a re-pick on failure. Re-measure with both slots populated; the stage-marker page is manifest B (fsbl/src/marker.rs:45), so today's harness can only measure the one-slot case.
4. ECC: delete "default handler = halt = recoverable by power cycle". A persistent double-ECC word halts every boot. Either add a minimal FSBL NMI handler policy or a silicon receipt showing what an interrupted erase reads as. This hazard already exists for the hashed range when BEGIN is power-cut mid-erase with the old inactive manifest still valid (manifest is erased last, secure/src/hw/flash.rs:1366-1386); it is untracked.
5. Add a third layer: blank-verify at BEGIN. erase_secure_page / erase_ns_page trust SR flags only (flash.rs:1307-1352). The COMMIT tail walk covers this for the tail; say so, and consider read-back after each erase as the direct fix.
6. Residual: add manifest-page slack and boot-state page 6 to the unchecked hiding places.
7. Sequencing: land the COMMIT half now (updatable, no FSBL budget). Land the FSBL half inside the #540/#758 cutover with CAP taken from pqsigner-geometry, and count its bytes against the Draft 1.1 rule of at least 2 KiB free in the 40 KiB region (a-b-firmware-rollback-architecture.md:276-277).
8. Part 2: do not have the secure-world row parrot the stored manifest digest. Recompute it (own image hash + NS hash + fw_version) or state the loss of the divergence signal as an explicit owner trade. Specify the monolithic-bench fallback. fwmeasure / `make measure` (Makefile:2254-2255) take the secure ELF only and must change in the same commit. Draft 1.1 review question 22 requires identical FSBL/secure-world fingerprints; keep that parity.
9. Part 2 belongs with manifest-v6, where the FSBL already computes the 121-byte preimage digest. Doing it on the legacy v1 FSBL is throwaway work.

skeptic.untracked_delta: Untracked, confirmed by search: (1) erased-tail check in fsbl::verify_images; (2) erased-tail check at CMD_FW_COMMIT; (3) explicit tail-erased assertion in verify-ship-state; (4) fingerprint derived from the manifest digest in all three renderers plus fwmeasure; (5) `make release` emitting expected words per slot. Added by this review, also untracked: (6) no blank read-back after page erase at BEGIN (flash.rs:1307-1352); (7) the FSBL has no NMI/ECC handler, so a persistent double-ECC word in any range it reads halts every boot (pre-existing for the hashed range, widened by the walk; silicon behaviour of an interrupted erase unmeasured); (8) bench flash recipes must erase whole slots once the check exists. One issue search ("fingerprint NS image") timed out and was re-run under different wording.
decision_conflicts: Invariant #10 / halt-never-write (2026-07-23): honoured, but the claim that fall-through avoids a brick is false for a one-slot device; a dirty tail there is a permanent halt at RDP-2.

Draft 1.1 (a-b-firmware-rollback-architecture.md:276-277): a production FSBL must keep at least 2 KiB free in the 40 KiB region; #758 already disputes headroom. The walk's bytes must be measured against that, not against today's 10,532 B free in the legacy 32 KiB link.

Draft 1.1 lines 274-275 and review question 22 (line 5454): fingerprint changes are outside the minimum rollback series and FSBL/secure-world fingerprints must stay identical. Part 2 changes the measured input, so it needs its own owner decision and must preserve parity.
